title: Sort the blocks by colour (Unitree G1, fixed pelvis, Pink IK)
text: 3 coloured wooden blocks (45 mm cubes) lie scattered on a work table: 1 red, 1 blue, 1 green. On the table are 3 marked coloured zones, one per colour (red and blue and green). Goal: sort every block into the zone whose colour matches it — put each block fully onto its matching-colour zone. A block left off the zones, or placed on the wrong colour's zone, does not count.
success: Success, exactly: each of the three 45 mm blocks (red, blue, green) has its centre within 55 mm horizontally of the centre of its own colour's zone, its centre height within 20 mm of resting on the table (table top 0.70 m + 22.5 mm, i.e. between 0.7025 and 0.7425 m), and moves slower than 0.05 m/s. The zone centres judged are this episode's, in the world frame: red (-0.1130, -0.3295) m, blue (-0.0143, -0.3168) m, green (0.1234, -0.3211) m; the coloured mats are drawn at (-0.11, -0.33), (0, -0.33) and (0.11, -0.33) m, so a judged centre is up to 20 mm off its mat's centre [scene._zones: the nominal zone_pos shifted by up to +/-15 mm per axis at reset]. Not true at the start (blocks lie behind the zones).
